newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open firmer, outperform U.S. issues.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open firmer, outperform U.S. issues.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened firmer on Thursday, with spreads to U.S. long bonds narrowing, helped by a firmer Canadian dollar and the absence of government bond auctions in Canada today, analysts said.

"The dollar has had a second straight day of upticks so that's certainly a factor here," said Hank Cunningham, director of fixed-income with First Marathon Securities Limited. "The market is very thin, I'm not seeing much of a bid here."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.26 to C$110.31 to yield 7.123 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 7/32 to yield 7.01 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to 11 basis points from 12 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.

Canadian bonds outperformed as the dollar opened stronger at C$1.3785 (US$0.7254) after rallying overseas trading. Traders said the dollar benefited from a market belief that the governing Liberals had consolidated their electoral strength days before the June 2 national ballot.
The Canadian market also benefited from the fact that there will be a U.S. five-year note auction today but no auctions in Canada. Canada held a five-year auction yesterday.
However, the Bank of Canada will release details of the Government of Canada's real return bond auction on June 4. The bond auction details will be released at 1530/1930.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.28 to C$102.98 to yield 6.573 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 6/32 to yield 6.77 percent.
The negative spread between the two bonds widened to 20 basis points from 18 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.99 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.10 percent.
